steps.notes: Empty header def tensor(): (D1); reduce-kron *args impl passes all 3 tests; column-ket '2d' reading fails (probe).
1-based subsystem indexing unstated (D4): sys=[2], dim=[2,2]; 1-based passes, 0-based probe fails.
General 2n-qubit impl passes; tests only exercise n=1, n=1-hardcoded probe also passes (D8); corrupted step ref 'in .'
Targets verified by hand (test1 diag(0.3,.05,.05,.05)/0.45); background formula rho''=V rho' V^dagger is dimensionally backwards (D10 minor); no-normalization probe correctly fails.
Squared Uhlmann fidelity ||sqrt(rho) sqrt(sigma)||_1^2 pinned by background; targets 0.25/0.5/0.0 verified analytically.
All 5 targets reproduced (0.5648, 0.8893, 0.9759, 1.0, 0.5); test 2 feeds complex Kraus despite 'floats' docstrings throughout the chain (D9).

findings.evidence: function_header is literally 'def tensor():' — ZERO parameters — while every test calls it with positional args: 'tensor([0,1],[0,1])', 'tensor(np.eye(3),np.ones((3,3)))', 'tensor([[1/2,1/2],[0,1]],[[1,2],[3,4]])'. The docstring does say 'args: any number of nd arrays of floats', so the intent (*args) is recoverable, but a model implementing the header as given produces an uncallable function (TypeError). Recurring empty-header pattern, identical to confirmed defects 11.3 and 19.1. My 'def tensor(*args):' reduce-np.kron implementation passes all 3 tests (steptest joint PASS).

Docstring promises 'M: the tensor product (kronecker product) of input matrices, 2d array of floats', but the h5 target for test 0 (tensor([0,1],[0,1])) is the 1-d int array [0 0 0 1] (shape (4,), dtype int32) — i.e. plain reduce(np.kron) output, not 2d. Probe: coercing 1-d inputs to column kets (the natural quantum reading of '2d') FAILS test 0 (np.allclose (4,1) vs (4,) broadcasts to a (4,4) comparison); flat kron and row-2d coercion both PASS. Same docstring/target mismatch as confirmed 11.3 D10.
findings.suggested_fix: Docstring: 'M: tensor (Kronecker) product of the inputs; np.kron semantics — 1-d if all inputs are 1-d'.

findings.evidence: Neither prompt, docstring ('sys: list of int or None, list of subsystems to apply the channel'), nor background states whether subsystem indices are 0- or 1-based. Test 2 calls 'apply_channel(K, rho, sys=[2], dim=[2,2])' — only consistent under 1-based (QETLAB-style) labels. Verified dynamically: 1-based implementation PASSES all 3 tests; the identical implementation with 0-based labels FAILS test 2 (AssertionError; with 0-based labels position 2 does not exist among {0,1}, so the channel is never applied — or index-error in list-based implementations). Pythonic default is 0-based, so a competent solver must guess. Same pattern as confirmed 11.4/11.8/11.9.
findings.suggested_fix: State in docstring: 'sys: list of int, 1-based indices of the subsystems the channel acts on'.

findings.evidence: Spec requires handling an arbitrary 2n-qubit input ('n uses of channel1' on the first n qubits), but all three test cases use 4x4 states (n=1). Probe verified: an implementation that hardcodes n=1 (apply_channel on sys=[1] then sys=[2] with dim=[2,2]) PASSES step 65.3 (steptest joint PASS), even though it crashes on the 16x16 (n=2) states used by 65.4/65.6. A non-general solution gets a false-positive at 65.3 and the failure is mislocalized to 65.6.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one n=2 test case to 65.3 (e.g. the 16x16 GHZ input from 65.6 with the dephasing channel).

findings.evidence: Prompt has a corrupted cross-reference: 'Implement a function that returns the output state using the apply_channel function in .' — the step reference after 'in' was dropped (stripped markup; same corruption family as confirmed 11.6/11.11/11.12). The function name apply_channel survives, so intent is recoverable.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the reference: '...using the apply_channel function from step 2.'

findings.evidence: Background defines V as a 2^n-row by 2-column matrix ('with 2^n rows') and then states 'The tranformed state is rho''=V rho' V^dagger'. This is dimensionally impossible: V rho' V^dagger requires rho' to be 2x2, but rho' is the 2^{2n}-dim post-measurement state (or 2^n per party). The intended operation is the adjoint direction, rho'' = (V tensor V)^dagger rho' (V tensor V), which reproduces all three h5 targets (verified: test 1 target diag(0.3,0.05,0.05,0.05)/0.45). A solver is forced by dimension-checking to flip the formula, so scores are unlikely to flip, but the stated formula is wrong as written.
findings.suggested_fix: Background: write rho'' = V^dagger rho' V per party, i.e. (V tensor V)^dagger rho' (V tensor V) on the full state.

findings.evidence: Test 2 feeds complex Kraus operators (y_error: np.array([[0,-1j*np.sqrt(0.1)],[1j*np.sqrt(0.1),0]])), but every docstring in the chain declares real dtype: 65.2 'K: list of 2d array of floats', 65.3/65.6 'channel1: kruas operators ..., list of (2,2) array of floats'. Probe verified: an apply_channel written strictly to its own float contract (preallocated 'np.zeros(rho.shape)' accumulator) PASSES all of 65.2's own tests but crashes 65.6 test 2 with 'numpy UFuncOutputCastingError: Cannot cast ufunc add output from dtype(complex128) to dtype(float64)' — step 65.6's test relies on complex support that 65.2's spec contradicts (out-of-contract test input pattern, cf. 29.1). Dtype-agnostic implementations (sum() accumulation) pass; targets themselves are real.
findings.suggested_fix: Change docstrings to 'array of floats or complex' (Kraus operators are generically complex), or replace test 2's y_error channel with a real-Kraus channel.

findings.evidence: Prompt cross-reference corrupted: 'Calculate the achievable fidelity ... using the protocol in given by the function ghz_protocol.' — a step reference between 'in' and 'given' was dropped. Function name survives, intent recoverable.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore: '...using the protocol in step 4, given by the function ghz_protocol.'

overall_assessment: Physics and targets are sound: all six steps were reproduced exactly by a literal-reading expert implementation (steptest joint PASS on every step, including the integrated 65.6 chain), all h5 targets were verified against hand calculations, and test strength is adequate (missing renormalization in 65.4 correctly fails). The two score-relevant defects are recurrences of the known quantum-info family patterns: the zero-parameter header 'def tensor():' (65.1, D1 major) and unstated 1-based subsystem indexing in apply_channel (65.2, D4 major) — both verified dynamically with both interpretations. Remaining issues are minor: doc/target dtype-and-shape contradictions (1-d target vs '2d' docstring; complex test input vs 'floats' contract that can crash a docstring-faithful solver at 65.6), a dimensionally backwards isometry formula in 65.4's background, weak n=1-only coverage in 65.3, and two corrupted cross-references. With the two major fixes applied, the problem is fair to score.
